sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for filter rules
sections.what: Brings in the saved data types and the capex band helper used by the filters.
sections.why: Setup code for the rest of the file.

sections.name: Filters
sections.title: Shape of the filter settings
sections.what: Lists every filter the owner can set: account, industry, solution, trigger, confidence, tier, audience, kind, status, theme, free-text search, region, country, capex, signal type and company. A blank value means the filter is not applied.
sections.why: Gives one shared list of filters for the page, the defaults and the matching logic.
sections.watch_out: A new filter must be added here and to the defaults, or it will not reset and may not be applied.

sections.name: INITIAL_FILTERS, normalize, validLocation, locationsOf, regionOf, countryOf
sections.title: Default filters and location cleaning
sections.what: Sets the starting filters, which show only open signals. Defines two special codes: one for signals with no tracked client and one for unmapped signals. Cleans text for comparison, checks that coordinates are real numbers in range, and returns the valid locations with fallback labels for missing region or country.
sections.why: Likely reason: bad coordinates should be dropped quietly rather than placed on the map.
sections.watch_out: The default status filter hides resolved and dismissed signals, which can look like missing data at first.

sections.name: industryOptions
sections.title: Industry dropdown options
sections.what: Builds the list of industries shown in the dropdown from the saved industries, the custom codebook industries that are in use, the account sectors and the signal industries. Duplicates are merged by a normalised name and the list is sorted alphabetically.
sections.why: Likely reason: the dropdown should offer every industry a visitor could filter by, even when the saved list is incomplete.
sections.watch_out: Entries with the same normalised name overwrite each other, so the last one added is the one the dropdown shows.

sections.name: filterSignals
sections.title: Applying every filter to the signals
sections.what: Keeps only the signals that pass every active filter: account, capex band, industry, solution, trigger, confidence, tier, audience, kind, signal type, company, theme, status, region, country and free-text search. Geography can be skipped for map views.
sections.why: Likely reason: one central filter keeps the list, map and counts consistent.
sections.watch_out: An empty filter means all, and the default status filter hides closed signals. The free-text search reads many text fields, so a long search across a large list may feel slow.

sections.name: regionCounts
sections.title: Counting signals by region
sections.what: Counts how many signals fall in each region. Signals with no sourced location go into an unmapped group. The regions are sorted by count, then by name.
sections.why: Gives the counts shown beside each region choice.
sections.watch_out: A signal with locations in two regions is counted once in each, so the totals can add up to more than the number of signals.

summary: Holds the filter rules for the Opportunity Map: the list of filter settings, the default state, the industry dropdown options, the logic that decides which signals pass the filters, and the region counts.
purpose: Decides which signals the owner sees for any combination of filters, so the list, map and counts all agree.
why: Likely reason: keeping all filter logic in one file means the list, map and counts all use the same rules. The code does not state this.
how: 1. Defines the filter settings and their empty default. 2. Cleans location data so only valid coordinates count. 3. Builds the industry dropdown from saved data, codebook and accounts. 4. filterSignals keeps a signal only if it passes every active filter. 5. regionCounts counts signals per region, with a group for unmapped signals.
inputs: The list of signals, the saved workspace data, the current filter settings, and an optional flag to skip geography filters.
outputs: The filtered signal list, the industry options, and region counts sorted by size.
risks: The default status filter hides dismissed and resolved signals, so a visitor may think signals are missing. A signal with several locations is counted in each of its regions. A new filter setting must be added in several places or it will be ignored.
debug: If a signal is missing, check each filter in filterSignals, and check the status filter first. If a dropdown option is missing, check the saved industry and codebook lists. If region counts look too high, check for signals with several locations.
